title: Average coordinate influence bound
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube in dimension $n>0$. Then some $i\in[n]$ satisfies $I_i(f)\ge I(f)/n$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
replaced:
For $n > 0$ there exists a coordinate $i$ with
$\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge I[f]/n$, the trivial averaging bound.
